text:
sara: FYI — customer reported sudden p99 latency regressions and intermittent request failures starting ~2026-03-14T09:12Z. They’re calling model-repro-v2 (8k) on us-east-1 shared pool. trace=tr_9a7e11b. Root symptoms: normally p99 ~150ms, spiked to >2.5s and a handful of requests returned 500s with ‘CUDA out of memory’ in worker logs. They repro by replaying long prompts in rapid succession.

maria: Can you paste the exact worker log snippet and an example request? Also confirm whether this customer is on hosted or dedicated.

sara: Hosted, org=acme-corp. Example payload: single-turn prompt ~4.8k tokens. Worker log (redacted):
```
2026-03-14T09:15:02Z worker-47 ERROR runtime: cudaErrorOutOfMemory: out of memory
  File \"/opt/runtime/serve.py\", line 395, in process
  File \"/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/cuda/alloc.py\", line 102, in allocate
```
Not every slow request hits OOM — seems intermittent.

lee: Classic sign: per-request KV cache growth + allocator fragmentation. Large-context requests populate big KV caches and long-tail or stuck requests hold memory. With many different allocation sizes, the CUDA caching allocator fragments, so even though total free memory looks nonzero, contiguous blocks for big allocations may be unavailable -> OOM.

devon: Did ops-bot roll out allocator telemetry? We need cuda_free_mb, cuda_total_mb, cuda_fragmentation_pct, kv_cache_count per worker.

ops-bot: allocator-telemetry deployed to us-east-1 at 2026-03-14T08:40Z. Metrics exposed: cuda_total_mb, cuda_free_mb, cuda_fragmentation_pct, torch_alloc_bytes, kv_cache_entries.

lee: I pulled the graphs for worker-47. Timeline: fragmentation_pct rose from ~10% at 08:30 -> ~72% by 09:10. kv_cache_entries on that worker climbed from ~150k -> ~1.9M in the same window. torch_alloc_bytes showed spikes coincident with large requests.

maria: That matches customer replaying long prompts quickly. Two-pronged mitigation: reduce incoming concurrency and switch their traffic to a lower-memory variant. Can we route acme-corp to model-repro-v2-quant while we investigate?

sara: Done — I updated org routing at 09:22Z to the -quant variant. Customer reports p99 dropped to ~350ms immediately and no further OOMs. They confirmed improved UX.

lee: Short-term runtime mitigations we should canary:
  1) PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64 (or 128) to reduce fragmentation.
  2) enforce kv_cache.max_entries_per_worker: 1_000_000 and add LRU eviction.
  3) implement per-request kv size check: if predicted KV size > threshold, respond with 429 + guidance to use quantized variant or smaller context.

devon: Local repro script I used to approximate the problem:
```
# fire many concurrent large-context requests (non-blocking)
for i in range(250):
  send_async_request(prompt=very_long_prompt(~4.8k))
# observe torch.cuda.memory_summary() and fragmentation metrics
```
On my dev node fragmentation jumped after ~80 concurrent inflight requests and p99 started to climb.

lee: For canary plan: create a tiny canary pool in us-east-1 (2 workers) with the allocator env change, route 3% of acme-corp + 1% random traffic, monitor p95/p99, cuda_fragmentation_pct, kv_cache_entries, and error-rate for 45 minutes. If good, roll to the rest of the pool with staged ramp.

maria: I opened a short-lived routing override for acme-corp (DONE) and filed CANARY-123 to test allocator config. I also set a temporary per-worker accept limit to cut concurrency by 40% so we avoid aggressive KV accumulation.

devon: Suggest we also add an automated rolling restart for workers that hit fragmentation > 60% sustained for 10m: drain (stop accepting new requests), let inflight finish up to 60s, then restart process. That will reclaim fragmented memory without a full machine recycle.

lee: Note: torch.cuda.empty_cache() does not defragment — it returns cached blocks but fragmentation remains. True defrag requires process restart or allocator-level compaction (max_split_size helps). We should also investigate allocator patches in newer torch releases; some improvements landed there.

maria: Risks of changing allocator config: it can increase small-allocation overhead or change latency distribution for tiny inputs. Canary and careful metrics are required. Also ensure our CI runs perf tests for both short and long contexts before full rollout.

ops-bot: canary deployment URL: https://canary-us-east-1.example.redwood/deploy/alloc-20260314 (deployed at 09:45Z)

lee: Longer-term roadmap items:
 - per-org KV quotas + billing signals for heavy long-context usage, alerting to SRE and account team.
 - smarter batcher that detects runaway KV growth and applies backpressure or forces large requests into a separate lane.
 - offload cold KV caches to host-pinned memory or CPU for enormous contexts on Dedicated/private, with read-through to GPU when needed.
 - allocator-aware memory compaction or leveraging upstream CUDA allocator features when available.

devon: I'll add a reproducible script to runtime/debug/soak_long_contexts.py and add documentation for support on how to run it safely against a canary pool.

maria: Action items (tracking ticket RUNTIME-457):
 - [maria] keep acme-corp on quant variant and notify them (DONE)
 - [lee] run canary with PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64 on 2 workers (IN PROGRESS)
 - [devon] add kv_cache_entries to org dashboards and create heavy-user alert (PR open)
 - [maria] create alert: cuda_fragmentation_pct > 50% for 15m -> page SRE (PR queued)
 - [lee] write rolling-restart runbook for high-frag workers (issue created)
 - [devon] land repro script and attach flamegraphs when reproducing (WIP)

sara: Customer is satisfied with the temporary fix and asked for ETA for permanent mitigations. Tentative ETA shared as ~2 weeks for KV eviction + allocator rollouts, subject to canary results.

lee: If anyone needs low-level inspection on a specific worker, run: 
```
kubectl exec -it worker-47 -- bash -c "python - <<'PY'
import torch
print(torch.cuda.memory_summary(device=0, abbreviated=False))
PY"
```
It prints allocation buckets and free-block summary which helped me confirm fragmentation.

maria: Closing this thread; we'll reopen for postmortem once canary completes and we have final rollout decision. :white_check_mark:
